svg.text: mlx-bun inference chain: the modules and the features each one owns
Solid arrows: the request path at run time. Dashed arrows: built once at load from the model, the flags and the machine. Nothing below the scheduler decides anything at run time.
Each module implements its contract and never checks what another is doing: composition is the guarantee. Swap any box for another implementation of the same contract and the rest does not care.

g.text: Protocols in, streams out. Decides nothing about the
• Request shapes, prompt policy, SSE streaming,
• Tool-call and reasoning markers surfaced as API
• Borrows the engine; serve startup owns it
• Web UI and /api routes belong to app modules,
• Chat templates and the family's chat defaults
• Vision preprocessing: images to patches and soft
Resolves the composition once from model + flags +
machine, then builds everything the scheduler runs.
• Composition: device, ANE bridge, KV scheme
• Graph table: the most-constrained graph wins;
exactly one generic graph per family
• Family records: marker tokens, chat defaults,
• Drafter loading: MTP head, DFlash 2 basis,
• LoRA adapters mounted onto named targets
• Grammar constraints: JSON schema or grammar to
• Seeded draws: key derived from (seed, step);
only the token id crosses to JS
The only component that decides at run time.
one request is a batch of one
• Names the phase and width: prefillChunk,
• Dispatches prefill chunks to the GPU or the ANE:
the ANE is a compute unit it manages
• Mixed iteration: prefill rows and decode rows in
adaptive depth over the built widths
• Asks the cache for prefix hit or miss; KV
• Row sampling: hands each row's logits to the
A second graph proposing tokens; the target verifies
• Built by the loader; reads the target's KV and
hidden states through its TargetView ports
• Drafts through grouped rows (one request is a
group of one); the scheduler verifies
One entire graph per model x quant x machine. Extends nothing; never inspects its input or its cache.
• Generated: Qwen3.8-27B Trellis 3.2bpw (M4 Pro, M1 Max), Gemma 4 e4b / 12B / 26B
• Generic, one per family: Qwen3 / 3.5 / MoE, Gemma 4, MiniCPM5, GLM-5.2, Llama (universal dense), DiffusionGemma, Whisper
• Phases: prefillChunk { gpu, ane }, prefillTail, decode / verify / appendKnown / logits width tables
• makeCache(): composes the cache lego its composition names
• Layer captures: residual basis and hidden taps for drafters
• Declared capabilities: vision, audio, draft head, pooled embeddings; vision and audio towers
Owns storage and the read. Answers hit or miss.
tiled; TurboQuant dense / deferred; KV4 head-256
• The read: attend(q, scale); masks memoized once
• Paged rows and row layouts for batching; row
• Prefix reuse (prefix cache, tiered); SSD offload
• Eviction and retention policy, KV budget, leases
• Snapshots and rollback for speculative verify;
• Delayed quantization legos take their kernel set
The blocks a graph is made of. Each imports the kernels it needs.
• Attention: Qwen3, Gemma, KV4 decode, quantized-append; the read strategy is cache.attend
• GatedDeltaNet recurrence; MLP: SwiGLU, GeGLU, Trellis gate-up / down, affine
• Linears: dense, quantized, Trellis (variant 13), switch (MoE experts), affine-verify
• Embeddings (dense, quantized); norms (RMS, layer norm); softcap
• RoPE, mRoPE, 2D RoPE; LoRA application on named targets
• ANE prefill split: instance-owned programs for exactly the chunk size
• Per-layer MLX compile choice (measured, never an app option)
• attention: fused SDPA, KV4 decode attention,
• quantization: affine quant / dequant, qmv, steel
• trellis: codebook decode, fused gate-up / down,
• delta: gated delta rule; glm52: MLA
Produce or consume the chain; they are not on the request path.
• @mlx-bun/quantize: the Trellis quantizer, publishes the one quant per tier (Qwen3.8-27B-Trellis-3.2bpw) | @mlx-bun/training: LoRA and ORPO on the graphs and state contracts | @mlx-bun/mlx: the
• App modules: chat (Pi, sessions, tool approvals), web, jobs, hub, memory (vault, synthesis), datasets, quantize and train jobs, metrics, models, transcription
